messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The provided test case testEscapeHtmlHighUnicode attempts to escape a high Unicode character (U+1D362) represented in UTF-8. The bug report states that characters above U+00FFFF are incorrectly converted into two characters during escaping. 

Examining the implementation of StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml(String), this method creates a StringWriter and delegates escaping to escapeHtml(Writer, String), which in turn calls Entities.HTML40.escape with the writer and the input string.

The critical fault lies in the Entities.escape(Writer, String) method. It iterates over the input string by char index, captures each char at position i, and attempts to get the corresponding entity name. If none exists, then for characters greater than 0x7F, it writes the HTML numeric entity using the decimal value of the char.

However, Java's char type is UTF-16 and represents only 16-bit code units, meaning characters above U+FFFF are encoded as surrogate pairs (two chars). Iterating char-by-char results in splitting such characters into two surrogate halves. Consequently, Entities.escape will treat each half as an independent character and write its numeric entity separately, rather than representing the entire Unicode character as a single entity. Specifically, the code converts each surrogate char's code separately with Integer.toString(c,10).

The test expects the high Unicode character U+1D362 to be escaped as "𝍢" but the current method improperly escapes it into two separate numeric entities corresponding to the surrogates, which is incorrect.

Hence, the root cause is that the escape method operates on UTF-16 code units (char) rather than iterating over code points to correctly handle characters above U+FFFF. Proper handling requires using codePoints or else manually identifying surrogate pairs and combining them to output a single numeric entity for the full character code.

This direct mismatch between UTF-16 char iteration and Unicode code point handling in Entities.escape leads to the incorrect escaping behavior seen in the test and reported in the bug.

Next, I will confirm the iterator style in Entities.escape by checking for code point handling or surrogate handling code.

Diagnosis:
The root cause of the bug is that the escape method in the Entities class iterates over the input string character by character (using charAt and char), which only processes UTF-16 code units. Unicode characters above U+FFFF are represented in Java strings as surrogate pairs (two chars). By handling each char independently, the method incorrectly converts each surrogate half into separate numeric HTML entities, leading to two characters in the output instead of a single one representing the full code point.

The test case fails because it expects the Unicode character U+1D362 (represented by a surrogate pair) to be escaped to a single numeric entity "𝍢" (the decimal code point value). Instead, the current code produces two separate entities corresponding to the surrogate halves.

To fix this, the escape method should iterate over code points (not chars) and convert full Unicode code points into the corresponding numeric entity, thus ensuring correct handling of characters beyond U+FFFF.

This explains why high unicode characters are not escaped correctly and cause the test failure.
